basis: snapshot narrativeCache.data — compact read: recommendation, coreAnalysis, pool openings, bridge, scenarios.

justifications.depth: Two pools totalling ~745 words. Core Collections explains the replenishment annuity and the vertical-integration margin, but neither pool derives a required volume, price or margin the way the Tesla and AMD reports do.
justifications.coverage: The two product segments are covered and the platinum pivot and tariff headwind are both quantified (200–250bp, 50–100bp transition cost), but geography and channel — where a jewellery retailer's risk actually sits — are absent.
justifications.logic: The mispricing claim is coherent: 10.9x forward EV/EBIT against a 14.1x historical average, with the cyclical trough attributed to silver and tariffs. It rests entirely on multiple reversion, and the report admits the allocation is a mechanical EBIT-proportional fallback that gives no premium to the growth segment.
justifications.evidence: Guidance ranges, gross margins and the Signet comparison are usable; the segment split is explicitly estimated rather than reported, and the report says so.
justifications.valuation: Three fundamental legs with no market anchor and a Base scenario below spot — structurally the cleanest part of the report — but the whole SOTP is a proportional split of one group multiple, so the parts add no information the group multiple did not already contain.
justifications.readability: Short, orderly and internally consistent; a reader gets the call quickly.

summary: The thinnest report of the set, and a fair illustration of the floor: on a two-segment consumer company the pipeline produces a competent multiple-reversion note rather than analysis. Nothing is wrong; little is proprietary.
issues: EV allocation is a mechanical EBIT-proportional split of the group multiple
No required-scale test in either pool
